diagnosis: All four rollouts revealed PF1, PF2, and PF3 via reveal actions and cited all three in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy problems. The gate failed solely because check C5 (linked to PF1, the privacy-notice update requirement) passed in only 2 of 4 rollouts. In every rollout the settlement mentions the privacy-notice update somewhere—either in the audience_vote_method decision value (rollout 2), in a commitment detail (all rollouts), or both—yet C5 still failed in rollouts 0 and 1. Comparing the passing rollouts (2 and 3) to the failing ones (0 and 1), the difference is not whether the privacy notice is mentioned but how it is encoded: rollout 2 embeds it in the audience_vote_method decision field, and rollout 3 uses commitment type "document_update" with explicit "update the audience-facing privacy notice accordingly" wording, while rollouts 0 and 1 bundle it into a single commitment with type "update" and a combined target like "show brief / privacy notice" or "show brief". This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: C5's threshold or expected field/wording does not match the natural variation in how models encode the privacy-notice update commitment.

C5.why: The updated platform terms change the voting method from ordinary phone-based or unrestricted voting to anonymous QR tokens and require the privacy-notice update.
